test_positive_g2_deg2_chi1.description: cvc5 SAT: Riemann-Roch for genus 2, degree 2 gives χ=1

test_positive_g3_deg5_chi3.description: cvc5 SAT: Riemann-Roch for genus 3, degree 5 gives χ=3

test_positive_trivial_bundle_g2.description: cvc5 SAT: Trivial bundle on genus 2 gives χ=1-g=-1
test_positive_trivial_bundle_g2.interpretation: Trivial bundle has negative Euler characteristic for g>1

test_negative_rr_formula_violation.description: cvc5 UNSAT: χ≠deg-g+1 AND Riemann-Roch holds simultaneously is impossible
test_negative_rr_formula_violation.reason: Riemann-Roch is a fundamental structural constraint; violation is UNSAT

test_negative_negative_degree_positive_c.description: cvc5 UNSAT: deg<0 AND χ>0 is impossible (negative-degree bundles have no sections)
test_negative_negative_degree_positive_c.reason: For deg<0 and g≥1, l(L)=0 and χ(L)≤0 always (no positive sections)

test_negative_multiple_chi_values.description: cvc5 UNSAT: same (g,deg) pair cannot yield two different χ values
test_negative_multiple_chi_values.reason: Riemann-Roch uniquely determines χ from (genus, degree)

test_boundary_special_divisor.description: cvc5 SAT: Special divisor deg=g-1 on genus 2 gives χ=0 (boundary case)
test_boundary_special_divisor.interpretation: Special divisors are the boundary of effective divisor classes

test_boundary_serre_duality.description: sympy: Serre duality relation χ(K)=deg(K)-g+1 for canonical divisor
test_boundary_serre_duality.interpretation: Canonical divisor has χ=1 for all smooth genus g curves

test_boundary_non_negative_chi.description: cvc5 SAT: For deg≥g, Riemann-Roch gives χ≥0 (non-negative Euler characteristic)
test_boundary_non_negative_chi.interpretation: Line bundles of degree ≥ genus always have non-negative χ, ensuring sections exist

test_boundary_canonical_divisor.description: cvc5 SAT: Canonical divisor for genus 3 has degree 4 and χ(K)=g-1=2
